hook: The thinker whose ideas of class struggle and communism shook the 20th century.

pages.x: Karl Marx was born in 1818 in Trier, in Germany. His father came from a family of rabbis, but became a Lutheran to keep his job as a lawyer. At university Karl was jailed for a night for drunkenness and fought a duel, then turned to philosophy.

The newspaper he edited in Cologne was shut down by the Prussian government in 1843. In Paris in 1844 he met Friedrich Engels, the son of a factory owner. They became partners in work and lifelong friends.

In 1848 they wrote The Communist Manifesto: "The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles." It ends: "Workers of the world, unite!" It came out just as revolutions swept across Europe.
Thrown out of one country after another, he settled in London in 1849, in two small rooms in Soho. Three of his children died young. Engels sent him money from his family's cotton mill in Manchester.

Day after day he sat in the Reading Room of the British Museum, filling notebooks about factories and money. He suffered from painful boils, and joked that the rich would remember them until their dying day.

In 1867 he published the first volume of Capital. It argued that factory owners grow rich from the unpaid work of their workers, and that capitalism would one day be overthrown by them. Engels finished it after his death.
Marx died in London in 1883. Only about a dozen people came to his funeral at Highgate Cemetery, where Engels said: "His name will endure through the ages."
Marx changed how people think about history, work and money. In the 20th century, communist states that claimed his ideas ruled a third of humanity, many of them as brutal dictatorships.
pts: Wrote The Communist Manifesto and Capital
